title: Deal four cards face down from a held deck: one hand holds it, the other slides only the top card off onto each place
instruction: Deal one card face down from the deck onto each of the four card places on the felt mat, then put the deck down on the mat.
context: Dealing cards is one of the most familiar table skills: anyone who has played a card game has dealt or watched it. The dealer holds the pack face down in one hand and takes cards off its top with the other, placing each face down in front of a player (pagat.com, Card Game Mechanics: "holding the pack, face-down, in one hand"; "removing cards from the top of it with her other hand"; "placing them face-down on the table"). A 0.3 mm card on a deck cannot be pinched by a gripper: it moves only by friction, a fingertip pressed on its back and pushed sideways, and it must come off alone (pressed too hard, the next card comes too) and land flat in its place, face down. One hand holds the deck level and low beside each place; the other pushes the top card out over the edge in short strokes until it tips onto the felt; then the first hand draws the deck back from under the card's trailing end, so it drops flat.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. (1) Card mat, fixed (taped down): green felt card-table cloth, 26 x 34 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at x 21.0, y -1.5. Four card places printed on it in white, each the outline of a poker-size card (63.5 x 88.9 mm, long side along y, 2 mm lines just outside it), centred at A (16.5, -9.0), B (25.5, -9.0), C (16.5, 1.0) and D (25.5, 1.0). (2) A deck of 52 Bicycle Standard playing cards (poker size, 63.5 x 88.9 mm, about 0.3 mm and 1.8 g each; the deck 15.6 mm tall, 94 g), loose, face down, squared, long side along y, centred at x 21.0, y 11.5 on the mat (its left end 4 mm past the mat's edge). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step the scorer reads the pose of the deck and of each separate top card, and each finger's collision-hull points. A card is in a place when half or more of its area is inside the outline and it is down on the mat (lowest point within 8 mm of the felt, not on the deck held above). A place is dealt when exactly one card is in it, with at least 80 % of its area inside the outline, face down (back up, tilted under 15 deg) and lying on the felt (underside within 2 mm). Two or more cards in a place: 0 for that place. Score: 0.25 per dealt place, at most 0.9 until the deck is set down and let go. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): all four places dealt, the deck resting flat on the mat (underside within 3 mm, tilted under 10 deg), every fingertip 15 mm or more from the deck and the dealt cards, and deck and cards still (under 1 mm in 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: an overhead photo at the end (cards counted per place; a transparent overlay marked at 80 % of a card's area; face down) and the video (deck down, let go); 48 cards left in the deck.
reset_notes: Pick up the four dealt cards, put them back on top of the deck face down, square the deck and lay it face down with its long side along y, centred at x 21.0, y 11.5 (tape marks at its corners). Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The lower 46 cards are one 9.6 mm block; the top six are separate cards at their true mass but 1.0 mm thick (true 0.3 mm, for stable contacts) and 4 mm narrower than the block, so the holding jaws squeeze only the block. Cards do not bend. Friction (estimates): card on card 0.20 static / 0.16 sliding, card on cloth 0.25 / 0.21, fingertip on card 0.35 / 0.33. The felt is a rigid 3 mm sheet.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms hovered over the table; the left gripper once came down beside the deck but never took it, and no card was dealt); demo: 1.0
